name: Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah
nameAr: شقيق بن سلمة الأسدي، أبو وائل، الكوفي
diedNote: in the caliphate of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz (99–101 AH), aged a hundred (Taqrib); Khalifah ibn Khayyat gives 82

taqrib.ar: ثقة مخضرم، مات في خلافة عمر بن عبد العزيز وله مائة سنة
taqrib.en: Reliable; a mukhadram (lived in both eras); died in the caliphate of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz aged a hundred.

verdicts.en: They agreed unanimously that he is reliable.

dhahabi.en: A mukhadram, one of the scholars who acted on their knowledge.

flags.label: Named by kunya here, by name elsewhere
flags.detail: Al-Bukhari writes “Abu Wa'il” in 3126, 2810, 123 and 7458; Muslim's routes through al-A'mash (1904b, 1904c), al-Tirmidhi 1646 and Ibn Majah 2783 give his name, Shaqiq ibn Salamah. Ibn Hajar lists him in Hady al-Sari among those famous by kunya whose name recurs.

bio: A Kufan who lived through the Prophet's lifetime without meeting him, and so is counted a mukhadram, and who lived to a hundred. A companion of Ibn Mas'ud and a narrator from Abu Musa, Umar, Uthman and Ali, he is the Successor through whom Abu Musa's report on fighting “so that the word of Allah is supreme” reached the Kufan school, by three different students: Amr ibn Murrah, Mansur and al-A'mash.

provenance.ref: Hady al-Sari, ch. 7, those famous by kunya
